title: The Dirt Trail Rivalry Just Got Ugly: 2027 Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk Vs. Ford Bronco Sport Sasquatch
excerpt: While the Jeep Cherokee was AWOL, the Ford Bronco Sport stole its thunder. Can it take it back?
content:
Published Oct 8, 2026, 9:09 AM EDT

James Kelly didn't grow up knowing he wanted to be a writer, but once he fell into the whacky world of automotive journalism, he hasn't wanted to leave. In college, he found ways to make every paper he wrote related to automobiles and even hosted a show on the campus radio station called "The Engine Block." James's experience involves road-testing brand new cars, breaking old cars, and everything in between. 

The Jeep Cherokee arrived earlier in 2026 after taking a three-year sabbatical to find itself. Now in its sixth generation, the Cherokee may look like it’s gone full city-slicker with its premium-looking interior and low-slung stance. However, the Trailhawk name returns for 2027 to change just that with some class-leading stats.

In that class is the Ford Bronco Sport, which put another two model years under its belt while the Cherokee was AWOL. Since its debut nearly seven years ago, it's become a force to reckon with – both on the road and on the trails. The Sasquatch package available on Bronco Sport models gives it a leg up out in the wilderness, but Jeep has a whole new machine ready to enter the fight.

Jeep Is Chasing Bigfoot With New Tricks

The original Bronco was Ford’s answer to the Civilian Jeep, launching both into a decades-long battle for SUV supremacy that continues today. The Cherokee is back to blocky looks, a design it hasn't worn since we called it the Liberty here in the US, and packs, for the first time ever, a hybrid powertrain. A 1.6-liter turbo-four churns an electrically-assisted planetary gear set that acts as a CVT, except it doesn’t have chains or belts. Instead, it uses the same engineering trickery as the original Toyota Prius to keep the engine in a prime torque band to move the wheels.

Better still, the four-wheel-drive system (standard on all Cherokees) is mechanical, unlike many hybrid systems that throw out the driveshaft in favor of a separate electric motor on the rear axle. Total system output is 210 horsepower and 230 lb-ft of torque, placing it smack between the two powertrain options for the Bronco Sport when it comes to power. The Cherokee has a manufacturer-estimated 31 combined MPG, putting it ahead of the Bronco Sport and a few other compact crossovers outfitted for trail use.

If you're stuck in the work grind that keeps your Cherokee from leaving the pavement, Jeep made sure it's the best one yet for daily use with good fuel economy thanks to a slick hybrid system. But that doesn’t mean it won’t hold up on the weekends when the fun begins. A low-range transfer unit provides a 2.92 low-range ratio and an impressive 37.5:1 crawl ratio, and a locking rear differential ensures power is sent where it's needed when teetering over uneven terrain. Not to mention 9-inches of ground clearance compared to the Bronco Sport’s 8.7 inches.

At $44,625 after a $1,995 destination fee, the base MSRP before features and options slots the Cherokee above Ford's offerings. The Bronco Sport’s pricey color options and other available packages can quickly match—and easily surpass—the price of the Cherokee. The Trailhawk will fit between the Limited Altitude and Overland when it officially goes on sale. Production will begin later this year at Stellantis’ Toluca Assembly Plant in Mexico, where it will be built alongside the Wagoneer S and Compass.

The Trails Await To Declare A Winner

We liked what the Cherokee had to offer when we drove it earlier this year, proud to report its ergonomic fixes and a larger – nearly grand – presence. It’s been stretched end-to-end over the old model and touts both a longer wheelbase and wider track thanks to its new STLA Large platform shared with the Dodge Charger and Wagoneer S.

It’s noticeably larger than its predecessor and over a foot longer than the Bronco Sport. The Cherokee’s larger construction and new platform returns a firm, confident ride that’s missing from the segment. Snappy steering and rock-solid road manners around Southern California’s coastal mountain roads were impressive, if not unexpected from a Jeep.

The low-cowl dashboard and airy interior provide good sightlines in traffic and excellent vantage points when negotiating unruly terrain. Our qualms were limited to the engine’s buzzy note when accelerating up hills and poor second-row comfort. Still, the rear seat room is far more capacious than the Bronco Sport’s, and where Ford littered its compact crossover with hard-touch plastics and cheap-looking trim pieces, Jeep has elevated its approach to interior design and material usage. The Bronco Sport, however, is as comfortable cruising on pavement as it is bouncing over jagged rocks, something we haven’t tested back-to-back in the Cherokee just yet.

On pavement, the Cherokee just might have a slight edge compared to the Bronco Sport. It has a weight advantage of almost 830 lbs over the Bronco Sport, a figure aided by its new architecture and 1.03-kWh hybrid battery, which keeps it planted but cuts into overall economy when rushed. But how will each hold their own on the trails? The sacred battleground for SUVs that wear nameplates that mean “try me” is sure to reveal all.

A Sum of its Parts: What Hardware Each Is Rocking

The Cherokee Trailhawk enters the fight with an extra inch of ground clearance (9 inches total) over standard models, along with 17-inch wheels wrapped in Nexen Roadian 245/65R17 all-terrain tires. The boost in height and knobby tires inflate approach and departure angles to 28.8 degrees and 31.8 degrees respectively. The Bronco Sport achieves a higher approach angle at 31.2 degrees, but fares worse with departure at 27.9 degrees. Ramp breakover angle for the Jeep is 21.9 degrees and 21.7 for the Ford.

The Bronco Sport Sasquatch is sprung with Ford’s high-performance off-road suspension (HOSS) 2.0 and gains an advanced four-wheel-drive system different than standard models. A twin-clutch rear drive unit mimics a limited-slip differential with the ability to cut power to the side that’s free-spinning.

Underbody protection is added, and 17-inch wheels fitted with P235/65R17 all-terrain tires bring the total clearance to 8.7 inches. Other mechanical changes include an 850W cooling fan bolted to Badlands models only to cool the 2.0-liter turbo-four.

These SUVs Work Hard And Play Harder

Not only has Jeep been the king of the trails for who knows how long now, but Ford really hit back with the full-fat Bronco and the tiny-but-mighty Sport model. Should anything wear either the ‘Jeep’ or ‘Bronco’ badge, it surely needs to deliver where it matters most. What that looks like today is a world apart from where these two started, but each knew exactly where it was going. As body-on-frame SUVs gave way to unibody construction, something the Cherokee gained as early as its second generation, the question then became "how will these vehicles live up to their names?"

Both the Cherokee and Bronco Sport are the epitome of the small SUV that needed enough chops to honor their family while also being soft enough to entrap more buyers. These two wear their names well and deliver on all the aspects buyers need and want in a new crossover. The Bronco Sport and Cherokee are the proper baby SUVs they’ve always been, sweetened only by the addition of off-road prepped models or available packages.

We like that the Cherokee is getting a Trailhawk edition, and it's certain to perform across all other terrain as well as it has on smooth tarmac. Ford’s decision to make the Sasquatch package available on two separate models rather than restrict it to a sole, standalone model is appreciated. But how the price of the cheaper Outer Banks can leapfrog the Badlands before other options are added is a decision we question. Jeep has painted a strong enough argument for us to believe the new Cherokee can dethrone the baby Bronco from its perch atop all other dirt-ready compacts, and we’re excited to put it to the test soon.
